args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate 0.18 across us-east, us-west, eu-west). Per the runbook, I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, in all production regions. Post-rollback status: all three regions on v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate 0.002. v2.3.1 is marked unhealthy in production and is not to be redeployed until it is fixed and verified. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 failure. Note that v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
checkout-api is rolled back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), and a SEV2 incident is open.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks in production with a 0.18 error rate. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. After the rollback, all regions report v2.3.0, healthy, with an error rate of 0.002.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, service checkout-api) is open and has paged the on-call engineer. The summary covers the rollback and notes that v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until it is fixed and verified. It also notes that v2.3.1-rc was unhealthy in staging.
- **Retry:** The first incident request timed out. I checked the incident list, found nothing had been created, and retried with the same idempotency key, so only one incident exists.

Follow-up for the on-call engineer: find the cause of the v2.3.1 failure before any redeploy.

content.text: The most recent production release that was healthy is v2.3.0. v2.3.1 is unhealthy in production and is currently serving in all three regions. Rolling back to v2.3.0.
